scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-01.statement: Tariff change log shows zero records.

F-03.statement: Field route completion for Aug‑Sep is 0.88, below the 0.95 target.

F-04.statement: Dispute volume monthly: June 610, July 590, August 1180, September 1260

F-05.statement: Dispute response median time 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, total tickets 2440.

F-06.statement: 14 lagging routes with low completion observed.

F-07.statement: 320 distinct accounts had estimated bills in the last billing cycle.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-WRONG-BILLS.statement: Dispute surge stems from incorrect bills (tariff misapplication, estimation errors, etc.) generated by the billing system.

H-AMI-READ-GAP.statement: Missing or delayed AMI reads from MDMS cause estimation substitution, producing inaccurate bills and disputes.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Field manual read process failures (missed reads, unconfirmed route changes) lead to estimation errors and disputed bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-SHIFT.statement: A change in billing import validation rules introduced in August caused systematic mis-billing that drove the dispute increase.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The tariff change log contains zero records, indicating no recorded tariff changes in the system during the period, which reduces the likelihood that tariff misapplication contributed to the dispute surge.
The observation shows more disputed bills for actual reads than for estimated reads, indicating that the dispute surge is not driven primarily by estimation errors.
Field route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating gaps in manual meter reads that could lead to estimation substitution and disputed bills.
The dispute volume rose from 590 in July to 1180 in August and 1260 in September, showing a clear increase during the disputed period.
The median dispute response time is 1.6 days, well within the 3‑day SLA, indicating that response speed is not a bottleneck; the high ticket volume (2440) reflects the dispute surge.

problem_definition.root_problem: A change in billing import validation rules introduced in August caused systematic mis-billing, leading to a surge in dispute tickets.

trace.summary: A change in billing import validation rules introduced in August caused systematic mis-billing, leading to a surge in dispute tickets.

structural_remedies.description: Rollback the billing import validation rule change to the pre-August version and reinstate the previous rule set.
structural_remedies.rationale: Rule change can be reverted via the billing-config tool within minutes; no automated bill writes required, satisfying K-BILLWRITE.; residual gap: Affected customers require bill adjustments/credits for the mis-billed amounts; this is a manual correction step handled by Billing Operations under existing authority.

structural_remedies.description: Institute a change‑control gate for any future billing import validation rule modifications (require review and sign‑off by Billing Operations before deployment).
structural_remedies.rationale: Adding a lightweight approval step can be documented and communicated quickly; does not involve protected bill writes.; residual gap: None – the root cause is eliminated and recurrence is prevented.
